mod-01.title: Module 01 Quiz — Introduction to Programming
mod-01.description: Test your understanding of programming, C++, Arduino sketches, and sequential execution.

questions.prompt: What language are Arduino sketches compiled from?
options: C++ with the Arduino core library
questions.explanation: Arduino IDE compiles standard C++ enhanced with hardware functions like pinMode and digitalWrite.

questions.prompt: Where is your compiled Arduino program stored so it persists after unplugging USB power?
questions.explanation: Flash memory is non-volatile; SRAM holds temporary variables that reset on power loss.

questions.prompt: What prints first and second?
questions.explanation: Statements execute strictly top to bottom: a is 3 on the first print, then updated to 7.

questions.prompt: Why is a 220-ohm resistor wired in series with an LED?
options: To limit current and protect both the LED and GPIO pin
questions.explanation: Without a current-limiting resistor, excess current can damage the LED and microcontroller pin.

mod-02.title: Module 02 Quiz — Computational Thinking
mod-02.description: Assess your mastery of algorithms, pseudocode, flowcharts, decomposition, and the IPO model.

questions.prompt: In the Input-Processing-Output model, what is a DC motor?
questions.explanation: Actuators like motors, servos, LEDs, and buzzers are Outputs.

questions.prompt: Which flowchart symbol represents an if/else decision?
questions.explanation: A diamond represents a true/false decision with YES and NO branches.

questions.prompt: Why should you test each sensor individually before combining 4 sensors into one robot?
options: It isolates hardware or wiring bugs quickly.
Arduino can only run one sensor.
questions.explanation: Decomposition isolates faults so debugging stays fast and systematic.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid pins D0 and D1 for LEDs/buttons on an Uno R3 when using Serial?
options: D0 and D1 are shared with USB Serial RX/TX.
D0 and D1 cannot be set to OUTPUT.
questions.explanation: D0/D1 carry USB Serial communication and sketch uploads on Uno R3.

mod-03.title: Module 03 Quiz — C++ Fundamentals
mod-03.description: Verify your command of syntax, data types, constants, arithmetic, comparisons, and casting.

questions.prompt: Which data type should ALWAYS store millis() timestamps?
questions.explanation: millis() returns a 32-bit unsigned long; 16-bit int overflows in ~32.7 seconds on Uno R3.

questions.prompt: What value does `int x = 9 / 2;` store?
questions.explanation: Integer division truncates the .5 fractional remainder.

questions.prompt: Which expression checks if temp is between 20 and 30 inclusive?
questions.explanation: C++ requires two separate comparisons joined by &&.

questions.prompt: What happens if your code tries to reassign a `const int LED_PIN = 8;`?
options: The compiler reports an error and protects the constant.
questions.explanation: const enforces read-only protection at compile time.

mod-04.title: Module 04 Quiz — Decision Making
mod-04.description: Test booleans, if-else chains, switch statements, and compound sensor guards.

questions.prompt: What prints if dist = 10?
questions.explanation: 10 < 15 matches first, prints STOP, and skips all remaining else-if/else branches.

questions.prompt: What happens if you omit `break;` at the end of a switch case?
options: Execution falls through into the next case.
questions.explanation: Without break;, C++ continues executing subsequent cases.

questions.prompt: Why write `if (dist > 0 && dist < 20)` for an ultrasonic sensor?
options: To prevent a 0 or -1 timeout error from triggering a false obstacle stop.
questions.explanation: Guarding dist > 0 ensures invalid timeout codes are ignored.

questions.prompt: Which operator tests equality without modifying a variable?
questions.explanation: == compares equality; = assigns a value.

mod-05.title: Module 05 Quiz — Loops
mod-05.description: Evaluate your skill with for, while, do-while, nested loops, break, and continue.

questions.prompt: How many times does this loop run?
questions.explanation: i takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — exactly 6 iterations.

questions.prompt: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least ONCE?
questions.explanation: do-while evaluates its condition at the bottom after the first run.

questions.prompt: An outer loop of 4 contains an inner loop of 3. How many times does the inner body run?
questions.explanation: 4 outer iterations * 3 inner iterations = 12 total executions.

questions.prompt: What does `continue;` do inside a loop?
options: Skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next iteration.
questions.explanation: continue skips only the remaining lines of the current pass; break exits the loop.

mod-06.title: Module 06 Quiz — Functions
mod-06.description: Check your understanding of parameters, return values, scope, and modular programming.

questions.prompt: What keyword indicates a function returns NO value?
questions.explanation: void specifies no return value.

questions.prompt: What happens to a plain local variable declared inside loop() on each cycle?
options: It is recreated and reset every time loop() starts again.
It retains its previous value forever.
questions.explanation: Use global or static variables for state that must persist across loop() cycles.

questions.prompt: Which parameter list is valid in C++?
questions.explanation: Every parameter must state its own type, separated by commas.

questions.prompt: Why use `long sum` when averaging 40 analogRead() samples on Uno R3?
questions.explanation: long avoids 16-bit integer overflow when accumulating many samples.

mod-07.title: Module 07 Quiz — Arrays and Data
mod-07.description: Test arrays, zero-based indexing, C-strings, structs, and enums.

questions.prompt: In `int pins[4] = {5, 6, 7, 8};`, what is `pins[3]`?
How do you properly compare two char array C-strings for equality?
questions.explanation: strcmp() compares the text contents and returns 0 when identical.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between an array and a struct?
options: An array holds one type; a struct groups fields of different types.
A struct can only hold ints.
Structs cannot be used on Arduino.
questions.explanation: Structs combine mixed types (int, float, bool) into one composite record.

questions.prompt: Why pair `enum` with `switch` in robotics?
options: It creates readable, compiler-checked state machines.
questions.explanation: Named enum states make Finite State Machines clear and bug-resistant.

mod-08.title: Module 08 Quiz — Advanced C++ Foundations
mod-08.description: Assess references, pointers, classes/objects, headers, .cpp files, and libraries.

questions.prompt: What does `void update(int &x)` allow the function to do?
options: Modify the caller's original variable directly.
questions.explanation: & passes a reference alias to the caller's variable.

questions.prompt: Why should Arduino classes call `pinMode()` in a `.begin()` method rather than the constructor?
options: Global constructors run before Arduino hardware initialization finishes.
questions.explanation: Calling begin() inside setup() ensures hardware timers and pins are initialized.

questions.prompt: What header must you manually include in standalone `.cpp` files that use `digitalWrite()`?
questions.explanation: Only .ino files auto-include Arduino.h; .cpp files must include it explicitly.

questions.prompt: What does `#pragma once` prevent in a `.h` header file?
options: Duplicate declaration errors if the header is included multiple times.
questions.explanation: #pragma once acts as an include guard.

mod-09.title: Module 09 Quiz — Arduino IDE Mastery
mod-09.description: Confirm you can verify, compile, upload, use Serial Monitor/Plotter, and troubleshoot Arduino IDE.

questions.prompt: Why might Serial Monitor display garbled random symbols?
options: The Serial Monitor baud rate does not match Serial.begin(...).
questions.explanation: Matching the exact baud rate (e.g., 9600 or 115200) fixes garbled serial text immediately.

questions.prompt: Can you click Verify (✓) to check for C++ syntax errors without an Arduino plugged in?
options: Yes — Verify compiles code on your computer without uploading.
No — a board must always be connected.
Only if Serial Monitor is open.
questions.explanation: Verify runs the compiler locally so you can catch syntax errors anytime.

questions.prompt: If no COM/tty port appears when plugging in a board, what is the FIRST hardware check?
options: Confirm the USB cable supports data transfer (not charge-only) and check drivers.
questions.explanation: Charge-only USB cables lack data wires and are the #1 cause of missing ports.

questions.prompt: What does Arduino IDE's Serial Plotter do?
options: Graphs numeric Serial data in real time.
questions.explanation: Serial Plotter visualizes live numeric telemetry as scrolling charts.

mod-10.title: Module 10 Quiz — Arduino Programming
mod-10.description: Test setup/loop, digital/analog I/O, PWM, millis(), and Serial.

questions.prompt: Why is `millis()` preferred over `delay()` in multi-tasking robots?
options: millis() lets the Arduino keep reading buttons and sensors while timing intervals.
delay() does not work in loop().
questions.explanation: delay() freezes execution; millis() tracks elapsed time without blocking.

questions.prompt: With `pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP)` and a button wired to GND, what does `digitalRead(2)` return when pressed?
questions.explanation: INPUT_PULLUP pulls the pin HIGH at rest; pressing connects it to GND (LOW).

questions.prompt: What value range does standard 8-bit `analogWrite(pin, val)` accept?
questions.explanation: Standard Arduino analogWrite uses 8-bit duty cycle values from 0 (off) to 255 (full on).

questions.prompt: On an Arduino Uno R3 (10-bit ADC), what range does `analogRead(A0)` return?
questions.explanation: 10-bit ADC produces 2^10 = 1024 steps (0 through 1023).

mod-11.title: Module 11 Quiz — Board-Specific Development
mod-11.description: Verify real hardware differences across Uno R3, Uno R4, Nano variants, Mega 2560, and ESP32 variants.

questions.prompt: Which board family uses STRICT 3.3V GPIO logic where 5V input signals can damage the chip?
questions.explanation: ESP32 silicon is strictly 3.3V logic; always level-shift 5V sensor outputs.

questions.prompt: On an Arduino Nano Classic (ATmega328P), what is special about pins A6 and A7?
options: They are analog-input-only and cannot be used with digitalWrite().
questions.explanation: A6 and A7 on Nano Classic connect only to the ADC multiplexer, not digital output drivers.

questions.prompt: How many independent hardware Serial UART ports does the Arduino Mega 2560 provide?
questions.explanation: Mega 2560 has 4 hardware UARTs, eliminating fragile SoftwareSerial for multi-device robots.

questions.prompt: Which ESP32 variant uses a single-core RISC-V CPU?
questions.explanation: ESP32-C3 is a low-power single-core RISC-V variant, distinct from dual-core Xtensa WROOM-32 and S3.

mod-12.title: Module 12 Quiz — Practical Robotics Programming
mod-12.description: Assess applied robotics wiring safety, sensor filtering, hysteresis, and motor control.

questions.prompt: Why must you NEVER connect a DC motor directly to an Arduino digital output pin?
options: Motors draw far more current than a GPIO pin can supply and produce inductive voltage spikes.
DC motors only run on AC power.
questions.explanation: Always use an H-bridge motor driver (e.g., L298N or TB6612FNG) with an external power supply and shared GND.

questions.prompt: Why does an automatic streetlight use two separate thresholds (e.g., < 350 ON, > 450 OFF)?
options: Hysteresis prevents rapid flickering when light hovers right at twilight.
analogRead only works with two numbers.
questions.explanation: A hysteresis deadband stops noisy borderline readings from rapidly toggling the lamp.

questions.prompt: Why do we divide the HC-SR04 echo distance by 2?
options: The sound pulse travels TO the object and BACK to the sensor (round trip).
Sound travels half as fast on Arduino.
questions.explanation: Dividing the round-trip travel distance by 2 gives the one-way distance to the obstacle.

questions.prompt: Why should multiple or high-torque servos be powered from an external 5V supply with shared GND?
options: Servo stall current can overload the Arduino's onboard 5V regulator and cause brownout resets.
questions.explanation: External 5V servo power with common GND prevents brownouts while keeping clean PWM signal reference.
